_comment: Hand-written plugins.json, the `after` half of checks.update-summary's case (b) (#49), paired
tests/fixtures/update/) as the locks -- so the lazy-nvim node's rev really does move
`pin` stays `true` (must NOT be dropped): update-summary.lua's classify() checks its
not is_true(after.pin)`. Dropping pin here would make the move classify as `(unpinned)`
instead of `(spec changed)`, defeating the point of this fixture (the plan's finding 2: an
unnamed, unrequested spec edit must not trigger the 'moved without being named' false
positive). `resolvedRef` goes back to null, the same way resolve.lua's own merge would react
to a spec identity change (a different `tag`) with no rev yet decided for it.
`tag`, which is what makes `same_identity` false and the reason `spec changed`.
